transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, hi. Yeah, I came in because I just... I can't stop feeling like I'm a danger and a total disappointment. There was this one near-miss at work, and it just proves I'm not meant to be a nurse. I mean, I worked so hard to get my RN so young, taking all those college classes early so I could start working by eighteen. My mom actually bought me this really nice rose gold stethoscope when I passed my boards. It's a Littmann, you know? The tubing is navy blue. She ordered it from this website that accidentally shipped it to our neighbor's house first, and Mr. Henderson—he's our neighbor, he has this massive golden retriever that always digs up our front yard—he actually had to bring it over to us. But... I don't know, I just look at it now and I just think everyone would be better off without me. Like I shouldn't even be allowed near a hospital.
Have you had other times in your life when you felt this low or down, or is this the first time you've felt this way?

Well, I guess... I think it's been about a year and two months now. It started right after I graduated high school. That was a really crazy time because I started my college classes and working full-time at the clinic all at once. Actually, the clinic is right next to this amazing little bakery, the one on 4th Street? They make these incredible blueberry scones. I used to go there every morning before my shift. The lady who runs it, Mrs. Gable, she always remembers my order. She has this cute little bell on the door that jingles every time someone walks in, and her grandson sometimes helps out on weekends. He's trying to get into nursing school too, actually. I gave him some of my old study guides. But yeah... it's been over a year of feeling like this. Ever since that whole transition started.
Have you had periods of feeling better in between times over the past year, or has your mood been consistently low throughout this time?

No, not really any better periods. It's pretty much constant. Like, most days I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. And I go to work and try to act normal at the clinic. Even when I'm smiling at patients in Spanish... which is actually something I picked up from my best friend in middle school, Sofia. Her family is from Mexico, and her abuela lived with them and she only spoke Spanish. She used to make us these incredible handmade tortillas from scratch every day after school. The whole kitchen always smelled like toasted corn, it was the best. They had this tiny little Chihuahua too, named Chico, who would always beg for scraps under the table. He had this weird little limp from when he jumped off their patio furniture too hard, but he was so sweet. He used to sleep right on my backpack. But anyway... yeah, even when I'm doing that, talking to patients and smiling and doing my job, I feel like I'm just barely holding myself together. The heaviness just doesn't really go away.
Have you ever had periods in your life where your mood was unusually high, you felt extremely energetic, or you were more irritable than usual for several days or longer?

Um, no, I don't think so. I'm never really energetic. I mean, unless you count being over-caffeinated, maybe? My coworker at the clinic, Sarah, she drinks those huge Monster energy drinks all day, the white ones with the zero sugar. She buys them in bulk and keeps them taking up half the space in the break room fridge. We actually just had to get a brand new fridge for the clinic because the old one completely died over the weekend and everything inside spoiled. It smelled so bad on Monday, like sour milk and old yogurt. Our clinic manager, Brenda, she was so mad because she had just bought this really expensive organic kale salad from Whole Foods and left it in there. Brenda is always doing these weird diets, actually. Like last month she was only eating things that were purple, so she kept bringing in all these eggplants and purple carrots, and her hands were literally stained from chopping beets... but, um, wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right. No, I don't ever get unusually high or energetic like that. Just... just the heavy feeling mostly.
Before this past year, have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks where you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Before this past year? No, I don't think so. High school was pretty okay before I graduated. Like, junior year I was actually super busy because I was on the prom committee. We did this whole "Enchanted Forest" theme, and we had to get all these fake trees from a theater supply place in the city. My mom drove us to pick them up in her old Subaru. That car is somehow still running, actually, even though the AC has been completely broken since like 2019. We drove all the way to Florida in it once for a family vacation, and it was so hot we had to keep the windows down the entire time we were on the highway. The wind was so loud we couldn't even hear the radio, and my brother kept complaining that his hair was getting messed up. He's so obsessed with his hair, he uses this special pomade that he has to special-order online from Australia, and it comes in these little tin cans with a kangaroo on them... um, wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, feeling down before all this. No, not really. I was usually pretty fine back then. It really just started this past year.
Have you ever had any previous episodes of depression before this past year, even if they were shorter or not as severe?

Um, no, not that I can remember. Like I said, it was mostly just this past year. I mean, middle school was a little rough, but that was just because of drama, you know? Like, there was this one girl, Chloe, who started a rumor that I cheated on a math test just because I got a higher grade than her. She was so competitive. She actually ended up going to the same community college as me for a semester, but she dropped out because she wanted to start a dog walking business. Which is crazy because she used to be terrified of dogs. Like, one time at a sleepover, my friend's golden retriever just walked into the room and she literally screamed and locked herself in the bathroom for twenty minutes. We had to slide pizza under the door to get her to calm down. It was pepperoni, from that place downtown that has the really good garlic knots... wait, sorry, what was the question? Oh, previous episodes. Yeah, no, nothing like this. Just normal teenage stuff before.
Have you had days when you felt so down or hopeless that you couldn't get out of bed, take care of yourself, or do your normal daily activities?

Um, yeah, some days are really hard. Like, I've completely fallen behind in my nursing prerequisites. I just can't focus on the coursework. And at work, at the clinic, I've had to ask my coworkers to double-check my tasks, things I used to do totally fine on my own. It makes me really scared to take on my normal responsibilities. Actually, my coworker Sarah—the one with the energy drinks—she's been really nice about it, but I feel bad asking her. She's already so busy because she's planning her wedding. She's getting married in a barn, which is super trendy right now, I guess. She showed me pictures of the venue and it has all these string lights and mason jars everywhere. They're having a taco bar instead of a regular sit-down dinner, which sounds amazing, but her future mother-in-law is apparently furious about it. She wanted them to have this fancy plated chicken dinner, but Sarah is vegetarian, so she refused. I tried going vegetarian once in high school, but I only lasted like three days because my dad made ribs and I just couldn't resist... um, wait, sorry. What were you asking? Oh, right, getting out of bed and stuff. Yeah, it's just been really hard to keep up with school and work lately. I just feel so useless there now.

Before this current period of feeling down, have you ever had a time when you felt depressed or lost interest in things for several days or more, even if it didn't last as long as this current episode?

Um, no, I really don't think so. Like I said, it's just been this past year that things got bad. Before that, I was fine. I mean, I had normal bad days, but nothing that lasted. I was always pretty busy, especially with work. I started at the clinic right after I finished my CNA program. The program was so intense, we had to wear these awful scratchy scrubs that were this terrible shade of maroon. Like, who looks good in maroon? And they were so stiff, even after washing them a million times. I tried using that fancy fabric softener that smells like lavender and chamomile, the one in the purple bottle? But it didn't help at all. My roommate at the time was allergic to lavender, actually, so I had to hide it under my bed so she wouldn't sneeze. She was allergic to everything, even dust. We had to vacuum like every single day. She had this vacuum that looked like a spaceship... wait, sorry. I'm doing it again. Um, no, I haven't had anything like this before. Just this time.

Before this current period of feeling down, have you ever had a shorter time — even just a few days or a couple of weeks — when you felt unusually low, hopeless, or lost interest in things you normally enjoy?

Um, no, I really don't think so. Like, I've never had a time where I just stopped caring about stuff before now. Even when things were stressful, I was always doing something. Like, I played softball for a bit in early high school. I actually ended up quitting after a few weeks, though, because the coach was just way too intense. He used to make us run bases in the pouring rain. One time, my friend Jessica slipped in the mud and completely ruined her brand new cleats. They were those bright neon pink ones that literally everyone wanted that year. Her mom was so mad because she had to drive all the way to the mall two towns over just to get them, since they were sold out everywhere else. That mall is actually closing down now, which is so sad because they had the best pretzel stand in the food court. They did these jalapeño cheese dips that were amazing, though they always gave me terrible heartburn... wait, I'm sorry, what did you ask me? Shorter times feeling hopeless? Right. No, I haven't had anything like that before this year.

Before this current period of feeling down, have you ever had any shorter times — even just a few days or a week — where you felt unusually low, hopeless, or lost interest in things you normally enjoy?

Um, no, really. I know you've asked a couple times now, but I honestly haven't. This is the first time I've ever felt like this, where everything just feels so heavy and pointless. Before this year, I was always pretty upbeat. Even when I got waitlisted for the nursing program the first time around, I was disappointed, but I didn't get depressed. I just decided to take a couple extra electives at the community college. I took this art history class that was actually super fascinating. The professor was this older guy with these crazy wild eyebrows, and he wore a different bowtie every single lecture. He had one with little tiny Mona Lisas on it. I tried to find one like it online for my grandpa for Father's Day, because my grandpa loves weird ties, but I couldn't find it anywhere. I ended up getting him this tie with little golf clubs on it instead, which he wore to my cousin's graduation. My cousin graduated with a degree in marine biology, which is so cool. She gets to work with sea turtles now down in Florida... wait, sorry. I'm doing it again, aren't I? Um, but yeah, to answer your question, no. Never before this year.
Have you ever had any other episodes of depression in your life, even if they were shorter or not as severe as this current one?

I feel like we're going in circles a bit, but no, I really haven't. I promise I'd tell you if I did. My memory is actually really good, usually, so I'd remember. Like, I can picture the exact layout of the grocery store my mom used to take me to when I was little. They had this huge row of those little plastic quarter machines right by the exit. I was completely obsessed with the ones that had those stretchy sticky hands in them? You know, the ones you throw at the wall and they just slap there and leave a weird greasy mark? My mom absolutely hated them because I got a red one stuck to the ceiling of her car once. It was a silver Honda, and the interior was this light grey cloth, so the stain literally never came out. She tried using dish soap and baking soda, which is actually a really good trick for getting stains out of scrubs, I learned that from one of the older nurses at the clinic... but it didn't work on the sticky hand grease at all. She ended up trading that car in a few years later anyway because the air conditioning died right in the middle of July and we were sweating to death... wait. I did it again. I'm sorry, my brain just keeps wandering off. But yeah, to be absolutely sure, no. I've never had any other times feeling like this before. Just this current one.

Have you ever had any days or weeks in your life before this past year where you felt down or hopeless enough that it affected your ability to enjoy things, even if it didn’t last very long or wasn’t as bad as this current time?

I know you keep asking this, and I feel bad because I feel like I'm frustrating you, but no. I've never felt like this before. Like I said, I usually have a really good memory for things. I remember almost everything. Like, I remember the exact smell of the library at my elementary school. It always smelled like dust and those old Scholastic book fair catalogs. I loved the book fairs so much. I'd always save up my allowance to buy those little spy pens with the invisible ink? The ones where you had to shine the little blue light on the paper to read what you wrote? I used to write secret notes to my best friend Sarah during math class. We thought we were so sneaky, but Mr. Henderson definitely knew. He was our math teacher, and he was so tall, he had to duck to get through the doorway. He actually played basketball in college, I think for some school in Ohio. My brother lives in Ohio now, actually. He moved there for a job in IT, but he hates the winters. He says the snow just turns into this gross brown slush everywhere... oh my gosh, I'm doing it again. I'm so sorry. My brain is just... it's like a TV changing channels on its own. But no, I haven't had any days or weeks like that before. This is all completely new to me.

Have you ever had any days or brief periods before this past year where you felt down or hopeless enough that it affected your ability to enjoy things, even if it didn’t last very long or wasn’t as bad as this current time?

I... I really don't know how else to say it, Doctor. No. I haven't. I feel like I'm failing a test or something because you keep asking the same thing, but the answer is still no. I've never had a time like this before. I'm usually the one who cheers other people up. Like when I was working as a CNA at the nursing home before I started my RN classes, I used to bring in my dog, Buster, on my days off. He's a golden retriever mix, and he just loves everyone. He has this one floppy ear that never stands up right, and the residents thought it was hilarious. Mrs. Higgins, she was this sweet lady who had dementia, she always thought Buster was her old dog from when she was a kid. She'd sneak him pieces of her breakfast sausage, which I probably shouldn't have let her do, but it made her so happy. Buster actually gained like five pounds that year, so I had to put him on this special diet food that smelled like fish. It was so gross. I had to keep the bag in the garage because the smell would just take over the kitchen. My roommate at the time, Jessica, she threatened to move out because of the smell. She was super dramatic about everything, though. Once she cried for an hour because they discontinued her favorite shade of lip gloss... wait. I'm sorry. I'm rambling again. I don't know why I can't just give you a straight answer without bringing up my dog. But no, I haven't had any brief periods of feeling like this before. It's just been this one time.

Before this current time of feeling down, have you ever had even a few days in a row where you felt unusually low or hopeless, even if it didn't last very long or wasn't as bad as what you're experiencing now?

I... I know you're asking about before, and I promise I'm not trying to be difficult, but I really just haven't. It's just now. It's just this time. Most days I wake up with this... this heavy, empty feeling right in my chest. And it's so hard because I'm trying to act normal at the clinic, you know? Like, I'll be smiling at patients, talking to them in Spanish because a lot of our patients at the clinic prefer Spanish. I learned it in high school, actually. My teacher, Señora Rodriguez, she was amazing. She used to bring in homemade tamales at the end of every semester, and they were the best things I've ever tasted. I tried making them myself once, but the masa was just completely wrong. It was too dry, and the corn husks kept tearing... I watched like three different YouTube tutorials, but I just couldn't get it right. My kitchen was a complete disaster area. There was corn flour everywhere, even on top of the fridge somehow. I had to scrub the floor twice because it got all sticky... oh. I'm doing it again, aren't I? I'm sorry. I just... I feel like I'm barely holding myself together right now, even when I'm smiling. But before this? No. Never.

Before this current time of feeling down, have you ever had even a few days in a row where you felt unusually low or hopeless, even if it didn’t last very long or wasn’t as bad as what you’re experiencing now?

I don't... I don't know why you're asking me this again. I really don't. I feel like I'm going crazy, like I'm speaking a different language or something. No. I haven't. I've never felt like this before. It's just been this one time. I'm usually such a happy person. Like, I love going to the farmers market on Saturday mornings. They have this one stand that sells these incredible honeycrisp apples. They're so sweet and crunchy, and the guy who runs the stand, he always wears these ridiculous hats. Last week it was a giant foam cowboy hat, and the week before that it was shaped like a piece of cheese. He said his daughter makes them for him, which is really sweet, actually. She's in art school in Chicago, I think. Chicago is so windy, though. I went there for a weekend trip once and my umbrella literally turned inside out and snapped in half. I had to buy a new one at this tiny little pharmacy, and it was bright pink with white polka dots. I felt so silly walking around with it... wait. I'm sorry. I'm doing it again. I'm just so tired, Doctor. But no, I haven't had any days like that before. Just now.

Before this current time of feeling down, have you ever had even a single day where you felt unusually low or hopeless enough that it affected your ability to enjoy things, even if it only lasted a few hours or wasn’t as bad as what you’re experiencing now?

I... no, Doctor, I haven't. Not even for a day or a few hours. I don't know why we keep going over this, I really don't. It's just never happened before all this started. I used to be the one who could find the bright side of everything, you know? Like when my car broke down last winter on my way to my morning classes. It was freezing, literally below zero, and the heater just stopped working. I had to wait for the tow truck for almost two hours, and I was wearing this huge puffy coat that made me look like a marshmallow. It was this bright metallic silver color—my mom bought it for me for Christmas, and she was so proud of it, so I had to wear it. She said it would make me visible to traffic, which I guess it did. The tow truck driver, he was this older guy named Hank, he actually gave me his thermos of hot chocolate while we waited for the paperwork. It was the best hot chocolate I've ever had, made with real milk, not that powdered stuff. He said his wife makes it for him every morning. They've been married for forty years, which is just incredible to think about. Forty years with the same person... I wonder if they still go on dates? My grandparents used to go dancing every Friday night until my grandpa's hip got bad... oh, God. I'm doing it again. I can't even hold a thought straight. I'm sorry. But no. No single days, no few hours. Just this current time.

Before this current time of feeling down, have you ever had even a single day where you felt unusually low or hopeless enough that it affected your ability to enjoy things, even if it only lasted a few hours or wasn’t as bad as what you’re experiencing now?

I... is this a test? Like, a memory test to see if my answer changes? Because I feel like you're not hearing me, or maybe you're reading someone else's chart. I really don't understand why you keep asking me the exact same thing. 

The answer is no. Not for a single day, not for a few hours, not ever. I was always perfectly fine before all of this started. Even when things were really stressful, I never felt hopeless. Being eighteen and doing nursing clinicals is incredibly intense, you know? The older nurses can be so tough on the students. There’s this one charge nurse, Brenda, who literally inspects our scrub pockets to make sure we have bandage scissors and the right kind of pens. She actually snapped at me once because I only had blue ink, and she insists on black ink for the patient whiteboards. I had to run all the way down to the hospital gift shop to buy a black pen, and the only ones they had left were those novelty ones with the giant fake flowers on top. So I had to walk around for the rest of my twelve-hour shift taking vitals with this huge, ridiculous pink sunflower bouncing around on my clipboard. One of the patients actually asked if he could keep it for his granddaughter. He was recovering from a knee replacement, and he had all these pictures of her taped to his tray table. She was dressed as a bumblebee for Halloween in one of them, it was so cute... 

Oh. God, I'm doing it again. My brain is just complete mush. I'm sorry. But please, you have to believe me. I never had any days like this before. It's only been this one time.

Before this current time of feeling down, have you ever had even a single day where you felt unusually low or hopeless enough that it affected your ability to enjoy things, even if it only lasted a few hours or wasn’t as bad as what you’re experiencing now?

I... I literally just answered this. Are you trying to trick me? I don't... I don't get it. I really don't. I'm telling you the truth. No. Never. Not even for an hour. 

I was completely fine before this. I loved my life. I mean, my apartment is tiny, but I love it. It has this little balcony that overlooks the parking lot, but if you look past the cars, you can see the tops of these really old oak trees. During the fall, the leaves turn this incredible shade of red, almost like a dark cherry color. I actually tried to paint them once. I bought all these watercolors from the craft store down the street, the one next to the bakery that smells like cinnamon rolls all day. The lady who works there, she always gives me an extra roll if I go right before they close. She says it's a crime to throw away good pastries, which I totally agree with. I took them to my study group once, and my friend Sarah ate three of them. Sarah’s the one who convinced me to get a cat, actually. She found this stray kitten under her porch and brought it over in a shoebox... 

Wait. Why am I talking about Sarah? I... I'm so sorry. My head just feels so foggy, like I can't hold onto a single thought. But please, Doctor, you have to stop asking me that. The answer is no. I've never felt like this before.
